course: If you are not a music major do not take this course. It's not a class where you can overcome every topic if you have no past in music theory.

The course is open to non-majors which in some ways could be something positive, but the class having students of so many different levels poses the problem of music majors not being able to get to the level of theoretical education they need/want. The topics are adjusted according to the average student taking the class and non-majors require the syllabus to be much easier/almost pointless for a music major. (comparing to the required levels of theoretical knowledge in Europe) The instructor compensates this lacking by being able to answer harder questions of more experienced-curious students but the foundation of the course still inhibits him from progressing more into the topic.

As a non-major student, I can say that the course really teaches you the fundamentals of music theory. It focuses on chords, harmony, and practical ear training. I personally think if you already know how to construct basic chords (like major, minor, or seventh chords—MM7, Mm7, m7, dim7 etc. — and their inversions) on a piano, and can identify them by ear, just attend the lectures and you'll be fine. I also highly recommend practicing interval hearing training on websites (such as "musictheory.net") regularly.
